chunks: Ḥabīb ibn al-Muʿallā asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and said to him:
Indeed, I am a man who is frequently forgetful, so I do not preserve my salat (prayer) except by means of my ring, moving it from one place to another.
So he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أُحَوِّلُهُ: I move it or shift it
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), meaning the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to move a ring during salat (prayer) to maintain attention?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a small physical action during salat (prayer), such as moving a ring, is permissible when it helps a person maintain attention and avoid forgetfulness. It reflects a practical legal ruling in worship and shows allowance for minor acts that support proper performance of prayer.
